# Dust Collector with Integrated Ironing Function

## Structural Overview

The dust collector consists of two main components: a bottom shell and an upper cover. The rear end of the bottom shell features an air outlet and houses a fan assembly, which contains both a fan and a stator. These elements work together to manage the airflow generated during operation.

## Airflow Channel Design

The fan assembly and air outlet are enclosed by a lower frame edge, creating a closed air flow channel. This enclosed design ensures that air moves efficiently through a controlled path before being discharged from the device, minimizing air leakage and maximizing performance.

## Heat Collection Mechanism

Within the air flow channel, a heat collector is positioned directly on the stator. As the device operates, this heat collector rapidly captures heat generated by the stator and transfers it to the passing airflow. Through this process, the air is warmed and transformed into hot air, effectively repurposing thermal energy that would otherwise be wasted.

## Integrated Ironing Function

Building on this heat collection system, the dust collector incorporates an ironing function. The hot air flow produced within the channel is directed to heat an ironing board, enabling the device to perform both ironing and sterilization tasks. This dual capability adds significant practical value to the appliance.

## Benefits and Advantages

This innovative design allows the device to recycle energy resources by harnessing heat that is naturally produced during operation. As a result, the dust collector can simultaneously perform multiple functions—dust collection, effective sterilization, and ironing—offering users an efficient, multipurpose solution that conserves energy while delivering versatile household utility.

# Dust Collector with Integrated Heat Recovery and Ironing Function

## Technical Field

The present disclosure relates to the field of household cleaning and garment care appliances, and more particularly to a dust collector that repurposes fan-generated heat to provide combined dust collection, ironing, and sterilization capabilities.

## Background

Conventional dust collectors operate by driving a motor and fan assembly at high speed to generate suction, drawing dust and airborne particles into a collection chamber. During operation, the fan motor and stator inevitably produce a significant amount of heat as a byproduct of their mechanical and electrical operation. In traditional designs, this heat is treated as waste energy and is dissipated into the surrounding environment, contributing to energy loss and, in some cases, uncomfortable operating temperatures. Meanwhile, tasks such as ironing and sterilizing garments typically require entirely separate appliances, each with its own energy consumption and storage requirements. This fragmentation of functionality increases both cost and household clutter, while the wasted thermal energy from vacuum devices remains unused.

## Summary of the Invention

The dust collector disclosed herein addresses these shortcomings by repurposing the heat generated during fan operation. This is accomplished by incorporating a heat collector positioned on the fan's stator within an enclosed air flow channel. As the fan draws air through this channel, the heat collector transfers the thermal energy produced by the stator into the passing air stream. In this way, ordinary airflow is converted into a heated airflow. This hot airflow is then directed toward an ironing board integrated into or associated with the device, providing the elevated temperatures necessary for garment care.

By capturing and redirecting energy that would otherwise be lost, the design enables the appliance to perform ironing and sterilization functions in addition to its primary dust collection role. The elevated temperature of the recovered airflow is sufficient not only to smooth fabrics but also to eliminate harmful microorganisms, thereby achieving effective sterilization. As a result, the device accomplishes dust collection and sterilization simultaneously, all while recycling energy resources that conventional appliances discard.

## Advantages

The integrated design offers several notable benefits. First, it improves overall energy efficiency by converting waste heat into a useful working medium, reducing the total energy demand compared to operating separate appliances. Second, it consolidates multiple household functions—vacuuming, ironing, and sterilization—into a single compact device, saving space and lowering the cost of ownership. Third, the sterilizing effect of the heated airflow enhances hygiene, offering added value in environments where cleanliness is a priority. Together, these features represent a practical and environmentally conscious improvement over conventional dust collection technology.

# ABSTRACT

## Dust Collector with Fan Heat Recovery System

A dust collector (10) that recovers and reuses waste heat generated by an internal fan assembly (20) to provide a heated air supply for garment care applications. The apparatus comprises a fan assembly (20) having a motor with a stator (22) and rotor (24), wherein the fan assembly (20) draws dust-laden air into the collector body (12) through an intake port (14) for filtration by a filter unit (16). A heat collector (30) is mounted in thermal contact with the stator (22) of the fan assembly (20), the heat collector (30) comprising a plurality of thermally conductive fins (32) configured to absorb heat generated by the stator (22) during operation.

Filtered air passing over the heat collector (30) is warmed and directed through a heated air duct (40) to an air outlet (50) positioned on the collector body (12). An ironing board (60) is coupled to the air outlet (50) via a coupling (52), the ironing board (60) having an internal air passage (62) and a plurality of perforations (64) formed in an upper working surface (66). Heated air received from the air outlet (50) travels through the air passage (62) and is expelled through the perforations (64), thereby providing steam-assisting warmth and moisture management during ironing.

In operation, the fan assembly (20) simultaneously performs dust collection and generates heat at the stator (22), which is captured by the heat collector (30) and delivered through the air outlet (50) to the ironing board (60), providing improved energy efficiency by repurposing otherwise wasted thermal energy.

# Abstract

A multifunctional cleaning apparatus integrating vacuum suction, garment ironing, and sterilization functions through the recovery and utilization of waste heat generated by a fan motor assembly. The apparatus comprises a housing containing a fan motor operable to generate an airflow for vacuum cleaning, wherein thermal energy dissipated by the fan motor during operation is captured by a heat-recovery module thermally coupled to the motor. The recovered heat is directed through a thermal conduction pathway to selectively supply a heated ironing surface configured for pressing and smoothing fabric articles, and to a sterilization chamber wherein the elevated temperature deactivates microorganisms, allergens, and other contaminants. A control unit regulates distribution of the recovered thermal energy among the ironing and sterilization functions in accordance with a user-selected operating mode, and may include one or more temperature sensors and thermostatic elements to maintain target temperatures within predetermined ranges. In certain embodiments, the airflow generated by the fan motor is diverted to enhance heat transfer, expedite sterilization, or provide steam generation for the ironing function. By repurposing otherwise wasted motor heat, the apparatus improves overall energy efficiency, reduces power consumption, and combines multiple household functions within a single compact device.

# ABSTRACT

## Multifunctional Household Appliance Combining Dust Collection with Thermal Energy Recovery for Ironing and Sterilization

A multifunctional appliance (10) is disclosed for integrated dust collection, garment ironing, and sterilization utilizing recovered thermal energy. The device comprises a housing (12) enclosing a suction assembly (20) having a motorized impeller (22) that draws particulate-laden air through an intake port (24) into a cyclonic separation chamber (26), where debris is deposited in a removable collection canister (28).

A thermal energy recovery module (30) is thermally coupled to the suction assembly (20) and comprises a heat exchanger (32) positioned adjacent the motor housing (34) to capture waste heat generated by the impeller motor (22). The recovered thermal energy is transferred via a conductive conduit (36) to a thermal reservoir (38) incorporating a phase-change material (40) for energy storage and stabilized heat delivery.

An ironing subassembly (50) includes a heated soleplate (52) in fluid communication with the thermal reservoir (38) through a distribution channel (54), whereby the stored thermal energy elevates the soleplate (52) to an operative ironing temperature. A steam generator (56) receives water from a reservoir (58) and utilizes the recovered heat to produce pressurized steam discharged through outlet apertures (60).

A sterilization unit (70) comprises an ultraviolet emitter (72) and a steam-diffusion nozzle (74) supplied by the steam generator (56), enabling microbial deactivation of fabrics and surfaces. A control module (80) with a microprocessor (82) and user interface (84) coordinates operation between the suction assembly (20), thermal recovery module (30), ironing subassembly (50), and sterilization unit (70), selectively routing recovered energy according to a user-selected operating mode.

The invention thereby improves overall energy efficiency by repurposing waste heat that would otherwise be dissipated, providing a compact, multifunctional appliance suitable for combined cleaning, garment care, and hygienic sterilization applications.

# Abstract

The present invention relates to a dust collector that innovatively utilizes waste heat generated by its motor and fan assembly to form a closed airflow circulation channel, enabling the simultaneous production of hot air for ironing applications. The device integrates a dust collection system with a thermal recovery mechanism, wherein heat dissipated by the fan motor during operation is captured and directed through a specially designed airflow passage rather than being expelled as waste.

The system comprises a suction unit for dust collection, a fan and motor assembly, and a closed-loop airflow channel that redirects the heated air generated during suction operations. As the fan operates to create suction for dust removal, the heat produced by the motor warms the incoming air stream. This heated air is channeled through an enclosed conduit and directed toward an ironing outlet, providing a continuous supply of hot air suitable for pressing and smoothing fabrics.

By forming a closed airflow channel, the invention prevents heat loss and improves overall energy efficiency, converting otherwise wasted thermal energy into a functional heat source. This dual-function design eliminates the need for a separate heating element for ironing purposes, reducing energy consumption and manufacturing costs.

The combined dust collection and ironing functionality offers a compact, multi-purpose household appliance that enhances convenience while promoting sustainable energy use. The invention is particularly advantageous for domestic and commercial cleaning applications where both surface cleaning and fabric care are required, providing an integrated solution that maximizes the utility of a single device.
